learning_outcomes.text: The student knows the basic principles of construction of modern computers, knows the rules of binary arithmetic (integer and non-integer), understand the causes of errors in the numerical calculations.
The student knows the basic principles of designing algorithms.
The student knows the basic principles of editing technical documents (style, including illustration, making presentations).

syllabus_topics: The program. Requirements. Outline of the history of the development of counting and computer systems.
Binary logic, basic arithmetic operations, computers calculations,
The operating system and its role. Different types of software (operating system, utility, ...)
Algorithms. The basic algorithmic structures (for review, the division of tasks, dynamic programming, recursion, ...).
Interesting use of computers (engineering graphics calculations)
Internet and related problems. Law and Internet.
assessment_rules: The concluding grade P is calculated as the average of forming evaluations F1, F2, F3, F4, F5: P = (F1+F2+F3+F4+F5)/5.
bibliography: Algorithmics: The Spirit of Computing (3rd Edition) by David Harel and Yishai Feldman (Jun 11, 2004)
Computers Ltd.: What They Really Can't Do (Popular Science) by David Harel (Dec 11, 2003)
Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach (6th Edition) by James F. Kurose and Keith W. Ross (Mar 5, 2012)
Operating System Concepts by Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin and Greg Gagne (Jul 29, 2008)
Algorithms + Data Structures = Programs (Prentice-Hall Series in Automatic Computation) by Niklaus Wirth (Feb 1976)
degree: Mechanical Engineering and Machine Building (I level, full-time)
